mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS spike (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% over the prior month coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as stronger wage growth supports consumer confidence and equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS acceleration (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weakening manufacturing demand and reduced equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO declines (p < 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and GDPC1 (demand and inflation proxies) above their 12-month averages is expected to produce a positive S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates a possible rate hold or cut.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite both proxies above average (p > 0.05 in F-test).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months indicates labor market slack, which is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate continued rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 3% is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as it reflects consumer spending strength and supportive equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative during RSAFS acceleration (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in HOUST (housing starts) by more than 10% in the prior quarter is expected to precede a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals cooling real estate demand and risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > -10% over the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS (employment) of 2% or more for two months is predicted to produce a negative S&P 60-day forward return as it suggests labor market weakness and reduced corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > -2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite employment decline (p < 0.05 in regression).
